newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA'S BULBANK TO PROVIDE $50-60 MLN TO BANKS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA'S BULBANK TO PROVIDE $50-60 MLN TO BANKS.

text.p: Bulgaria's state-owned Bulbank would provide $50-60 million for stabilisation of local banks in line with a financial accord with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister said.

"Bulgaria has found a way to provide immediate financing to support banks ahead of introduction of a currency board system in June. Bulbank will provide $50-60 million to the government to stabilise banks," Stefan Sofianski told reporters.
The decision was taken at today's session of the Financial Stabilisation Council (FSC). Two Bulbank executives are among its members.

Under arrangements with the IMF Bulgaria has to take immediate action to support two weaker state banks before an IMF board meeting in the second week of April expected to approve a $510 million stand-by facility agreed on Monday.

The IMF mission leader Anne McGuirk said on Monday that Bulgaria and the Fund had agreed on immediate steps to strengthen any weaknesses in the state banks and on financing resources of about $50 million for that purpose.

Under the accord signed on Monday Bulgaria is to introduce in June a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, the currency board system, to restore confidence in the national currency, the lev and bring the country back from the brink of default.

"Bulbank will provide the funds as a loan to be backed through proceeds from future privatisation deals," Krasimir Angarski, ecomony advisor to Bulgaria's President and also a FSC member, told reporters.

Stabilising state banks by boosting their capital prior to introduction of a currency board system has been seen as an alternative to future bank closures, a Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) official said.
"Bulgaria could not afford a third wave of banks closures," the BNB official told Reuters.

The BNB has put 15 local state and private banks or a third of Bulgaria's total in receivership since May 1996 and has sought their insolvency through the courts in two waves in May and October. Only one of them has been declared bankrupt so far.

State-owned banks now hold some 70 percent of Bulgaria's financial market and any new closures could dramatically erode confindence in the banking sector before the introduction of a currency board, the BNB official said.
Bulbank, where the state holds a 98.03 percent equity, is considered the biggest state commercial banks with total assets of 253.9 billion levs at the end of 1995.

Last year Bulbank sold to the government dollar-denominated domestic bonds worth $400 million for $180 million. The paper was transferred to seven state-owned banks in a bid to improve their negative capital net worth.
The $180 million were deposited with the BNB for five years and made part of its foreign exchange reserves, which totalled $445.5 million at end-February.
